Subject: Post-call: Fiscotech pilot economics & batching impact breakdown

Hi Anna —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. TL;DR: we heard performance pain at peak, unpredictable token spend, and a goal to get unit cost under $0.003/token while keeping p95 latency <400ms. Below is what we discussed and a pragmatic pilot recommendation focused on batching + prefix/KV caching to move the needle on TCO.

What you told us (pain & goals)
- Spiky traffic during settlement windows causes p95 latency to spike 2–3x and forces conservative provisioning.
- Current unit cost is ~ $0.006/token (open model hosting + burst infra).
- Priority: reduce per-inference $/token by ~40% without degrading UX (p95 target 350–400ms).
- Budget constraint: procurement wants to keep incremental Q3 spend below ~$45k.

Key levers we recommended on the call
1) Continuous request batching for user-facing flows: aggregate short requests to improve GPU utilization and amortize decode cost.
2) Prefix / KV caching for repeatable system prompts and common user prefixes (expected hit rate 15–30% depending on UI).
3) Quantized model variant for lower-cost baseline (ften small quality delta but large cost upside for high-volume tails).
4) Route low-SLO background reranks to a higher-throughput low-cost variant.

Back-of-envelope TCO assumptions (please confirm):
- 1,000,000 tokens/day baseline, avg sequence length 150 tokens, baseline $0.006/token.
- Caching (prefix hits): conservatively 20% of tokens avoided.
- Batching improvements: effective per-token compute reduction = 25% at 50% batch-able requests.
- Combined ballpark cost reduction: 35–45% (range because of cache hit uncertainty).

Proposed pilot (practical, low-risk)
- Scope: 4–6 weeks, two endpoints: (1) user-facing chat with batching + prefix caching; (2) nightly rerank routed to quantized variant.
- Volume target for pilot: start small (10k–50k req/day) and scale to sample 50k/day for representative economics.
- Deliverables: ROI slide, break-even at 10/50/100k req/day, production integration checklist, performance regression checks (QA prompts).
- Budget framing: expected pilot spend (estimate) $18k–$28k depending on scale and reserved capacity option.

Attachments: I’ve uploaded a short spreadsheet with the assumptions and a draft scope (fiscotech-pilot-econ.xlsx; proposed-pilot-scope.pdf).

Next asks / decision points
- Can you confirm the 20% prefix cacheable assumption is reasonable given the UI you described?
- Is a 4–6 week pilot timeframe acceptable to procurement?
- If yes, we can schedule a 30m kickoff next week to lock scope and share an ROI one-pager.

I’ll loop Marcus and Grace on operational checklists and SOW drafting. Thanks again — excited to help shape a low-risk path to material savings.

Best,
Soojin Lee

Anna / Andrew —

Thanks for the quick clarity. Attached is a concise break-even summary (fiscotech-break-even-summary.pdf) — top-level numbers below and assumptions so procurement can review quickly. I’ve also added a shared Drive link with the working spreadsheet and a one-slide ROI we’ll include in the kickoff deck.

Headline break-even (net $ savings vs baseline on-demand pricing) — conservative stacking of levers: batching + prefix cache + quantized rerank:
- 10k req/day (avg 150 tokens/req): ~18% net savings (~$0.0011/token net)
- 50k req/day: ~37% net savings (~$0.00095/token net)
- 100k req/day: ~49% net savings (~$0.00075/token net)

Key assumptions (short):
- Baseline: $0.006/token on-demand; avg seq 150 tokens; traffic distribution as discussed.
- Cacheable prefix: 20% (you confirmed 18–22%).
- Batching effectiveness: 25% compute reduction at our projected batch size.
- Quantized rerank: lower-quality variant for background jobs only (no UX impact).

Pilot budget options (choose one):
A) On-demand pilot: estimated spend $22k–$28k for ~4 weeks at 50k/day sample. Includes monitoring + regression checks.
B) Reserved mini-commit pilot: 1-month reserved block in exchange for a 10% pilot discount, estimated net $19k–$25k.

Yes — we can enforce an hourly spend cap / kill-switch on the pilot (we’ll expose it in the Console and also configure an automated cutoff at the account level). I’ll include the operational runbook in the kickoff pack so your ops team can validate.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marcus to share the 1-slide ROI and minimal SOW (by EOD Monday).
2) If procurement is comfortable, confirm pilot option A or B and a target kickoff window (we have availability week of Aug 24).
3) We’ll schedule a 30m kickoff and share the Drive folder + pilot checklist + DocuSign SOW draft if needed.
